source: BBOC 2026 Sun Belt Betting Preview (Stuckey/Mike Calabrese/Josh 'Duck' Nunn)
note: Layer-B numerics (sp_mar/sp_rank/ret_prod/TARP/6-Win%/SOS/miles) pending the 2026 edge+SP+ join; mkt_win_total and collin_proj are pod-stated. QB detail follows the 2026 enriched convention.

teams.qb_status: Battle (4-way, all new) — Camden Coleman (transfer, prev. multi-yr starter at Richmond, dual-threat game-manager) / J.C. Evans (transfer, mobile, had committed to Rich Rod at Jax State) / Matthew Maiden (transfer from Memphis) / Alonza Arrington [lead: hosts split — Evans favored by some, Stuckey + Calabrese think/hope Coleman wins; incumbent Alonzo Barnett left for UCF; Davis Belfort moved to WR]
teams.key_avoids: Opens Liberty (~TD fav) + Wagner (cakewalk), then back-to-back roadies at San Diego State + at Old Dominion (the early test); HOSTS Marshall (home/away split matters in the East race). After ODU, arguably favored in every game.
teams.bboc_notes: HOST SPLIT on the total — Calabrese OVER 8.5 (Billy Napier rehab hire, 33 wins in his last 3 UL Lafayette years, best resources in the league via ~$60M student-fee athletic funding; 2nd-rated G6 portal class; road-grader OL rebuild + deep RB room incl. Nick Herman, a 1,000-yд Drake back), Stuckey UNDER (+125) — downgraded them ~13 pts from year-end after Chesney left for UCLA and stripped the roster: 136th in returning production, 18 of the top-28 offensive+defensive snaps gone to P4/NFL, secondary a question. Duck: wait-and-see, need to see the offense; front-doors the East if they beat ODU + Marshall. 3-1 to win the conference.

teams.new_oc: Cody Cook (internal, ex-WR coach; first-time play-caller)
teams.qb_status: Returning backup — Colton 'Heinecke' (played some in 2024 incl. a shaky bowl vs USF; must develop as a passer — 'a mix of the old ODU Heineke throwing it around and Colton Joseph') [incumbent Colton Joseph left for Wisconsin; QB1 is unproven as a passer]
teams.key_avoids: Opens Norfolk State; at Virginia Tech (won 3 of last 7 vs Hokies — noise chance); ECU home (sneaky tough); then JMU; downspot at Georgia State after Va Tech. All five remaining road games winnable (Georgia State, App State, La Tech, Coastal, UConn). Weird late UConn trip (has a bye before it).
teams.bboc_notes: Both lean UNDER 7.5 (Stuckey projects 7.4-ish, no bet; Calabrese under). Ricky Rahne has built the culture, but the OFFENSE is the worry: lost QB Colton Joseph (Wisconsin), 3 WRs to P4, and the ENTIRE OL (all five started every game, 7,500+ career FBS snaps) — the 2026 line has ZERO career FBS starts (Elon C Braylan Walker + a JUCO LT). New first-time play-caller Cody Cook (Decker left for Memphis). Fell from 66th → 114th in returning production. Defense returns 8 of top-15 snaps (maybe the best LB group in the Belt) but the havoc creators/turnover luck (25 takeaways, 9th) may regress. 2024's 10 wins were schedule-timed; a real step back likely.

teams.new_dc: Brad Lambert (2nd stint; former Broyles nominee)
teams.qb_status: Returning — Carlos del Rio-Wilson 'CDRW' (incumbent, mobile; went 5-3 when he started AND finished games in 2024; hosts call him possibly the BEST QB in the conference) [backups Zion Turner + Khalil Wilkins limit the drop-off if he's hurt; RB-committee offense, only 119th in pass rate]
teams.key_avoids: Non-con at Penn State (+24.5, hang-around spot) then should blast Middle Tennessee + Gardner-Webb (Missouri State a red-ink revenge game). Great WEST draw (South Alabama + UL Monroe). BUT plays BOTH JMU and ODU on the ROAD — must split to reach the tiebreaker.
teams.bboc_notes: Stuckey's + Calabrese's dark-horse to win the East (~10-1; both take a shot; over 7.5). 2024 was a year-zero (Gibson took over after the whole team followed Charles Huff to Southern Mississippi — 75 new players) and they STILL went 5-7 with a 1-4 one-score record while out-gaining JMU/ULL/App State in losses — easily an 8-win team. Now a senior-laden offense in Gibson yr2, CDRW back, new DC Brad Lambert (a Broyles nominee in his first Marshall stint, elite situational D). 88th in returning production (highest in the East). The 2024 D was horrendous (bottom-10 in explosives allowed) — Donnie Smith (11 sacks) back + portal DL should help. Could be 6-1 before the ODU game.

teams.qb_status: Transfer — Max Johnson (transfer, Super-Sr, started at LSU in 2020 then Texas A&M/UNC; journeyman on his last stop, injury-prone) [backups: Turner/Tor Helton — the HC's son — plus Wes Brian, a short-yardage/wildcat runner; 'one play away from a disastrous offense']
teams.key_avoids: 2nd-toughest Sun Belt schedule (Duck). Non-con at Clemson, at Jacksonville State, Houston home; brutal East draw. HOSTS JMU + Marshall but goes to ODU. Could be 2-5 before it gets deeper.
teams.bboc_notes: A fade lean (Duck under 5.5 since spring; Stuckey/Calabrese pass, no path to the division). The offense was DECIMATED — all 11 players with 400+ snaps gone (QB JC French to Cincinnati, 3-yr RB Arnold, 3-yr WR Cobb, RT to Michigan State, C to North Texas). 108th in returning production (was top-50). They're rebuilding the O with P4 transfers (didn't pan out) and the D with FCS plug-ins. New DC Mike Mutz (SFA) is a pressure guy for a D that had 9 sacks all of 2024 (dead-last-ish pass rush) — the one real upside. QB is Max Johnson, who 'absolutely cannot stay healthy.' OL/DL maybe the worst aggregate trenches in the Belt. Not a bowl team.

teams.qb_status: Battle — Malachi Singleton (transfer from Purdue, ex-'MAC legend'/dual-threat) likely QB1 / Tommy Ulatowski (transfer from Kent State) / Henry Hasselbeck [lead: hope is Singleton, may use multiple; the 2024 room bled out — 40+ portal departures]
teams.key_avoids: Conducive slate — 4 home wins likely (Maine, Charlotte, Georgia State, UL Monroe), winnables on the road (at Coastal, at South Alabama). Easy West crossover (UL Monroe + at South Alabama). HOSTS JMU + ODU in Boone. Only ~3 games as a double-digit dog.
teams.bboc_notes: Under lean but a soft one (Stuckey ~5.0, right on market, passes; Duck leans under but the schedule is too winnable to fire). Program on the decline — 127th in returning production, 40+ portal losses, lost 9 of top-10 tacklers; hosts are not Dowell Loggins believers (rode the one good LaNorris-Sellers-fueled year at South Carolina). QB unsettled (Singleton the hope). Trench help: RT Poindexter back from injury + LT Manuel (Florida/Arkansas) should steady the tackles; RB room has pop (Jaquez Cross from Ark State, Jaquari Lewis). Pass D was shredded in 2024 and the FCS DB imports don't obviously fix it. Bowl needs a road steal or two.

teams.new_oc: (Bobby Petrino coaching tree — brought both coordinators)
teams.qb_status: Battle (wide open, no FBS starting experience) — [Trey] Bailey (transfer from Missouri State, wasn't the starter) / Tanner Lopez (freshman) / Jackson (freshman) / Trey Garra-Warren (JUCO All-American, was P4-recruited as a backup — LSU/FSU/Arkansas/Texas Tech interest — chose Coastal to play for Petrino) [lead: unsettled; Beard says all four in the mix; incumbent gone, full reset]
teams.key_avoids: 3rd-toughest Sun Belt schedule (Duck). Beats Fordham; crushed by West Virginia (Duck fades wk1, -17.5 → played to 22.5); at Delaware (dog), Liberty home. Horrific West draw (UL Lafayette + Arkansas State). Fade spots at Marshall, at UL Lafayette, at JMU. Four coin-flips (Georgia Southern home, App State, Georgia State, Ark State).
teams.bboc_notes: A FADE — both under (Stuckey projects 4.2, pays for under 5.5 / under 4.5 plus-money; Duck fades wk1). Full reset under new HC Ryan Beard (the Petrino-tree hire from Missouri State — Stuckey is skeptical of the nepotism-heavy staff and the 'lucked into Jacob Clark' Mizzou run; they didn't bring Clark). No FBS starting experience in a 4-way QB battle, a bad OL (both 2024 tackles left for Duke + Oklahoma State), and skill positions void of talent. The 2024 D was awful (474 yд/gm in conf, 130th in explosives allowed) and now leans on Missouri State DL transfers. Would need to sweep 4 coin-flips + steal one for 5 wins — unlikely. Calabrese's lone silver lining: watch JUCO All-American Trey Garra.

teams.qb_status: Returning — Christian Brown (incumbent, steadier option; 13:1 TD:INT in limited 2024 action, the clear best option over Finley — hosts puzzled he didn't play more; battled OL injuries around him) [QB play should be steadier + healthier in 2026]
teams.key_avoids: Winnable slate — opens FCS NC A&T (Duck's over play, 'shred them'); swaps Ole Miss/Memphis/Vandy off the 2024 non-con for Kennesaw, UCF, NIU (much softer). Draws JMU/ODU/Marshall run-heavy fronts that could 'run through them like tissue paper.'
teams.bboc_notes: Year 3 of Dell McGee — Calabrese + Duck lean OVER 3.5 (Stuckey ~3.9, wants to bet the over but the DEFENSE scares him). Coming off a 1-win year, but the OFFENSE should be much better: QB Christian Brown (13:1 in limited time) over Finley, a healthier/upgraded OL, and OC Hugh Jackson back — projects top-20 in pace + improved 3rd-down (81st in 2024). The problem is the defense — 9 new starters, still adding low-level bodies, could be one of the worst run Ds in the league (they lost 13 of top-16 snaps, oddly 7 to P4). Expect shootouts → a lot of Georgia State OVERS early before the market corrects (Duck's angle).

teams.qb_status: Returning (both back) — Goose Crowder (incumbent, injury-prone, health the whole question; sub-7 YPA / <8.5 aDOT in 2024) + Tucker Kilcrease (returning; a bit better) [new veer-and-shoot scheme adds tempo/RPO/motion — can Goose hit the deep shots it needs?]
teams.key_avoids: Should win every conference HOME game (Southern Mississippi, UL Monroe, La Tech, Georgia Southern). Starts 2-0 then tough road games; hosts Arkansas State in the finale (possible division decider).
teams.key_injury: Goose Crowder — durability; hasn't been able to stay healthy
teams.bboc_notes: A pass on the total (Stuckey ~market, no future; Duck projects 7.4-8 but doesn't love them). Contender in a WIDE-OPEN West (Stuckey has the top 5 within a field goal). Goes 19th → 119th in returning production but keeps BOTH QBs. New veer-and-shoot OC (from a high-scoring Tarleton State) with tight splits/slow-mesh RPOs — but the 2024 OL allowed a FBS-worst 59 sacks (injury-riddled; some guys who started at tackle project to 3rd-string now). Lost the top-6 WRs. The 2024 calling-card D graduated most of its front (Donnie Smith-type edge Chris Culliver-... gone; DE Donnie Smith-... ) — leans on DE Donnie Smith? no: keeps DE Donnie Smith equivalents + adds portal, but the DL basically graduated. High variance.

teams.qb_status: Returning — Walker 'Lunch' Winfield (incumbent, dual-threat/run-first; wasn't the planned 2024 starter but took over midseason and the offense averaged 34 ppg over the last 4 games once they balanced him; must develop as a passer) [ZERO QB depth — 'if Lunch runs and gets hurt, it's over'; the ONLY Sun Belt team with the same HC + both coordinators + QB]
teams.key_avoids: EASIEST Sun Belt schedule (Duck) — AVOIDS JMU, ODU AND Marshall; dream East draw (Coastal + Georgia State). HOSTS South Alabama, Arkansas State, Troy (huge in the West race); road at Southern Mississippi, UL Monroe, La Tech. 3 winnable non-cons (Lamar, UAB, Charlotte).
teams.bboc_notes: The West favorite (~8-1, Calabrese's 7-1 pick to win it) — Duck + Calabrese lean OVER 7.5. A 'grown-in-a-lab' develop-your-own roster: 81st in returning production (high for the Belt), 3rd in returning starts. Full offseason for Lunch Winfield + WR Shelton Sampson (a possible star capped by 46% catch rate on inaccurate 2024 QB play) + a big rebuilt OL (6 players back with 25%+ snaps, but most injury-plagued line in the country in 2024). The DEFENSE is the drag — DC Jim Salgado's unit was 100th+ in scoring/total D and returns only 2 starters; leaned on FCS imports (Tito Chikwelu, Broderick Stewart) to fix a 121st pass rush + 85th run D. Desormeaux is poor in one-possession games — situational execution is the swing. Stuckey out on Desormeaux + not sold on Lunch's arm.

teams.new_oc: Garrett Altman (from Vanderbilt, QB coach — slow-pace/Pavia-style)
teams.qb_status: Battle — Trey Owens (transfer from Texas, So, 6-5/225, high ceiling/physical tools, Super-Troopers mustache) — Stuckey's WANT and the projected UPGRADE [incumbent 3-yr starter Jaylen Raynor left for Iowa State; Owens the higher-ceiling swing over Raynor's win-games-lose-games profile]
teams.key_avoids: Manageable slate — dream East crossover (Coastal + Georgia State). HOSTS Troy in the finale (likely division-decider). Road-heavy winnables (at Southern Mississippi, at UL Lafayette, at Coastal, at La Tech) but they're 9-27 SU on the road since 2020.
teams.bboc_notes: Stuckey's West flyer (~11-1 vs UL Lafayette's 8-1 — the value play). Rare Belt team that RISES in returning production (100th → 82nd); nearly the whole OL back. The upside is the QB swing to Trey Owens (Texas) + new OC Garrett Altman (Vandy QB coach — expect a much SLOWER pace to protect a resetting D, which Duck flags as an unders angle vs Memphis/TCU/Kennesaw early). WR reload needed (Chancy Cobb, 70 catches, back). The DL that was decent graduated; the back-seven that returns (safeties) was BAD and gave up a ton of explosives (110th). Butch Jones' teams win a pile of one-score games (9 in 2 years) + elite special teams — the reason to buy in a coin-flip division. Duck: 'we won't go under.'

teams.qb_status: Returning — Bishop Davenport (incumbent; short/safe profile — 6.38 aDOT, 2.7% big-time-throw, 5% turnover-worthy: poor ratios even for a checkdown passer, doesn't push it deep) [freshman Hollins waiting in the wings — hosts would be MORE interested if Davenport struggles and Hollins takes over; not framed as an open battle]
teams.key_avoids: 3rd-easiest Sun Belt schedule (Duck) — should beat Southeastern UL Lafayette + winnable home games. Losses at Tulane, Auburn/Kentucky-type non-con, at Marshall, at UL Lafayette. The question is whether they steal a road game they shouldn't to reach 6-6.
teams.bboc_notes: A FADE — all three effectively under (Stuckey projects ~5.6, right on the number, wants the under; Calabrese under plus-money). Trend line down (10 → 7 → 7 → 4 wins). Major Applewhite hit the panic button — calls his own plays now + hired DC Todd Orlando (a blitz-heavy 'break-glass' hire whose FAU/USF Ds relied on fluky takeaway luck, not a sustainable calling card). Roster got worse basically everywhere (OL, RB, WR, TE, LB, DBs all downgraded; only ~2 assistants retained), no NIL money, and the passing game fell off a cliff post-Gio-Lopez. Red-zone D was horrific (41/43 trips scored on). Real chance of a midseason firing. Calabrese wants Southern Mississippi to cash his late-season fade tickets against them.

teams.new_oc: (new OC — an offensive-line coach; expect run-heavy)
teams.qb_status: Battle — Trey Kucuk (Kukuk) (incumbent-ish, returning from injury, should be healthy) vs a lean into the run/option [2024 became an option team out of necessity — only 8 passing TD all year; no clear WR talent to throw to, so the new OL-coach OC may just run it]
teams.key_avoids: Steps UP into the Sun Belt from CUSA (but travel drops from ~5,500 to ~2,050 miles). Tough open (at LSU, at Baylor, Army home, then UL Lafayette) — a likely 1-3 start. 4-27 SU on the road since 2021; road at Troy, at South Alabama, at Georgia Southern not assured.
teams.bboc_notes: Lean under (both ~market; Duck likes the DK ALT under 6.5 at -166 as value). #1 in the Sun Belt in returning production, but a hollow-looking group: 2024's 8 wins came against a parade of bad teams (Sela, NMSU, USM, UTEP, Sam Houston, an overtime Liberty, backups-vs-Coastal in the bowl) — a Cumby job-saving mirage. The passing attack never materialized under Sonny Cumby (only 8 pass TD); the new OC is an OL coach → likely full run commitment, but the interior OL (RG/RT/C) is a question and there's no WR talent. The D loses 8 of the top-10 tacklers + real star power. A real step up in competition; Duck projects a 1-3 start.

teams.qb_status: Battle (unsettled, ~99% new roster) — multi-way incl. Ethan Hampton / Landry Lyle / a returning QB4 from 2024 [no established starter; possibly the most walk-on/replacement OL in the country — protection is the bigger problem than the QB]
teams.key_avoids: Bad crossover draw (JMU + at ODU). Favored vs Alcorn; likely loses at UConn (wk3). Home games (ULL, JMU, South Alabama, La Tech, Arkansas State) — most winnable is UL Monroe but it's ON THE ROAD. Where are the 4 wins?
teams.bboc_notes: A hard FADE — Stuckey UNDER 3.5 (plus money), Duck already in the app under 3.5. Roster is ~99% new: lost the top-15 defensive snaps (7 to Memphis, 3 to P4), and the entire senior-laden offense from the Charles-Huff year left (Huff's staff/players went to Memphis). [Transcript is ASR-garbled on the coaching picture — it names 'head coach Blake Anderson' for 2026, implying Anderson was elevated as Huff's group departed; flagged, not asserted with confidence.] The DC is an elevated special-teams coach handling total turnover. Most-walk-on OL in the country. No path to 4 wins on the board. Sell.

teams.qb_status: Battle (unsettled) — Aiden Armenta (returning) / Austin Carlyle (transfer from Houston) / Landon Graves [lead: unsettled — 'doesn't know what they want to be offensively'; QB health is huge]
teams.key_avoids: Only remotely-competitive 2024 conf games were vs rivals Arkansas State (lost 15 straight to them before) + UL Lafayette. Slow-pace, ball-control to protect a bad D.
teams.bboc_notes: Fade lean (Duck under; Stuckey pessimistic — 'no money at all' in the program). Brian Vincent's best team but that's a low bar: near-zero offensive explosiveness (scored ≤14 seven times, topped 200 pass yds only twice, 13 red-zone TD all year, ~100th in explosiveness), and RB Bam McReynolds leaving is huge. Unsettled QB battle (Armenta / Houston transfer Austin Carlyle / Graves). Lost 3 more OL starters. Special teams were 'the worst I've ever seen' in 2024 (couldn't hit a 20-yд FG — all the kickers got hurt); brought in 3 kickers, so it can only improve. LB is the lone bright spot. Slow tempo to hide the D. Surprised Vincent is still around.
